differentiator: oh-my-pi anchors every edit to the content hash of the surrounding code, not to a line number, so the edit lands on exactly the right place or it is rejected.

color_script.secondary: oh-my-pi's own dark terminal surface #100e18 as inset code panels (the night inside the day) - these are the SOLID dark elements the light-canvas readability gate needs
color_script.accent: deep rose #920864 for text-scale hash/anchor marks; bright rose #dd389d for glows on dark panels; success-green #5fd37f (lands) and a danger-red (#e5484d) at the duel; cyan #00dbe4 as the cool IDE accent
temperature_beats: warm rose lock at the money shot
color_script.brightness: light canvas => bright by construction (crawl4ai's light run hit mean luma 217); >=30% bright is trivial; every scene carries a solid dark panel or bold dark headline so readability has real coverage

concepts.name: The Duel (CHOSEN)
concepts.world: An editor's desk rendered as warm technical paper; the code itself lives in dark terminal panels inset on the page.
concepts.shows: A file shifts underneath two pending edits. The line-number edit lands where line 47 USED to be and corrupts the file (red). The content-hash edit re-finds its exact target by fingerprint and locks in clean (rose). Side-by-side, the pictures ARE the argument.
concepts.money_shot: the side-by-side flip: left corrupts, right locks, at the same instant the file moves
concepts.creator_repost: Can is a reverse engineer - anchor-to-content, distrust-positions is his native instinct. Seeing his editing idea dramatized correctly is flattering to the exact audience he respects.
concepts.stranger_stop: every AI coding tool paste-edits and sometimes wrecks a file; the duel shows a fix you can feel in one glance
concepts.argument: head_to_head is the clearest dual-coding available: the viewer SEES why content-anchoring beats line-anchoring without a word of explanation. The split is the money device; the anchor motif (concept B) folds in as the setup beat; the locksmith idea (concept C) is a reference, not a scene.

concepts.name: The Anchor
concepts.world: one sustained metaphor - a rose content-hash anchor glyph that clamps a code block
concepts.shows: the anchor grips the code; the file changes; the anchor either holds (content still matches) or releases cleanly (content gone) - never corrupts
concepts.money_shot: the anchor clamping with a precise click
concepts.why_not: beautiful but single-threaded - it shows content-anchoring works but never contrasts it with the line-number failure, so the WHY is weaker than the duel

concepts.name: The Locksmith
concepts.world: the hash as a key cut to exactly one lock
concepts.shows: the key turns only when the code (the lock) matches the hash; wrong code, key won't turn
concepts.why_not: cute but one metaphor-step too abstract for a systems audience; git's content-addressing is the truer reference and it stays a touchstone, not the frame

wow_bets: the side_by_side_flip money shot: file shifts, left edit corrupts red, right edit re-locks rose, on the same beat
a precise click (foley click_minimal) landing ONLY on the lock - the mechanism you can hear
